post.description: Adds new entries, updates existing ones and marks entries missing from the file as no longer in the game. Importing the same file again changes nothing.

post.summary: Import the node table the map tool writes (resource-nodes.json, ADR-0015)
post.description: Adds new nodes, updates existing ones and marks nodes missing from the table as no longer in the game. The game version comes from the table.

get.summary: One import: game version, time and what it changed
Items, optionally only one form: ?form=solid or ?form=fluid
Recipes with their per-minute rates, optionally only those that produce an item (alternates included)
Belt, lift and pipe tiers with their capacity per minute
Resource nodes and resource well satellites from the map, optionally only one resource: ?resource=Desc_OreIron_C
Everything the player places, by class name, with the name the game shows
Miners and extractors with what they extract per minute on a normal-purity node at 100% clock speed

post.summary: Import a save file (.sav) as a new world snapshot
post.description: Every import is kept. Recipes the Catalog doesn't know are listed in unknownRecipes; buildables that aren't modelled yet in unsupported. Its analysis is computed in the background: analysis says pending until it's ready.

get.summary: One snapshot: when it was saved and imported, what it contains, and what the import couldn't place

delete.summary: Delete a snapshot and its analysis
delete.description: The world's factories stay: they belong to the world, and are traced in its next snapshot (BR-W2). An analysis still being computed for it is dropped.

post.summary: Define a factory in a world by its machines (BR-W2)
post.description: A factory belongs to a world (a session name) and is traced in every snapshot of it. Its machines must be machines or generators in the world's latest snapshot, and none of them another factory's.

get.summary: The factories defined in a world: ?world=<session name>
Every factory of the snapshot's world, traced in this snapshot (BR-W3, BR-W11)

post.summary: What chosen machines would make a factory in this snapshot, before it's saved: the logistics it would own and its outputs and inputs (BR-W3, BR-W4)

get.summary: The findings of a snapshot: every machine, why it runs below 100%, bottlenecks, unused supply, and sources of unknown rate
get.description: Computed in the background after the import and stored (ADR-0017): 202 with status pending until it's ready. Rates per minute, to 4 decimals. Every list starts with the worst. A finding in a part of the world that didn't settle is marked approximate.

get.summary: The findings of one factory in a snapshot: what it makes, its machines and belts, and the suppliers that feed it (BR-A14)
get.description: Made from the snapshot's stored analysis: 202 with status pending until that's ready. Not found when the snapshot or factory doesn't exist, the factory belongs to another world, or its output belt isn't in this snapshot (BR-W11).

get.summary: What the world map draws of a snapshot: its machines and providers, where they stand
get.description: Positions are in the game's units (centimetres). How each machine runs comes from the snapshot's analysis.
